questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly until the traffic moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up and you cannot get completely through. Wait until the traffic ahead clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will give you space to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will give you space to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even when you signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: When following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop when following these vehicles at railroad crossings.

questions.question: An oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get attention. If the other driver does not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left because the other driver may correct and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the crash impact.

questions.question: When a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes starts to lose grip on a slippery road, the driver should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle loses grip on a slippery road, press hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can. Releasing the pedal or pumping the brakes will turn off the system.

questions.question: When visibility is reduced, your first action should be to:

options.text: Look for road edge markings to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down should be your first action when visibility decreases or road conditions become dangerous.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones unless a different sign is posted?
questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 25 miles per hour. Follow any posted speed limit that is different from this.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a lane is ending and you should prepare for traffic to merge safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead, slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will curve right and then left. Slow down before you reach these curves.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they will stop. If you are following this driver, be ready to slow down.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show directions and distances.
questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show directions and distances to help you find where you need to go.

questions.question: How do you avoid glare from an oncoming car's headlights?

options.text: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the centerline of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road. Then look ahead to watch where the other car is.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should not:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another way to your destination.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your correct exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway. Continue driving to the next exit or turn. Other drivers do not expect cars to back up, and this will likely cause a crash.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on everything except:

options.text: How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: How physically fit you are.
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. It does not depend on your physical fitness or how well you think you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the wheel.
Next to each other on top of the wheel.
One on top and one on bottom of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and allows you to turn safely.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow X on a reversible lane sign mean?

options.text: The signal will change to a red X soon.
The signal will change to a green arrow soon.
You may only use this lane to turn.
You may drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only use this lane to turn.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow X means you can only use this lane to make a left turn. Lane control signals show which lanes are open and closed.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black text. They warn you about conditions ahead that may not be obvious.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.
